summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video: Introduction to Animation p02 2_Optimizing Animation ## Introduction In this segment, we will explore how to optimize animations in Marvelous Designer by making adjustments to costumes and understanding the impact of physical properties on animation stability. ## Stabilizing Animation Now we have a model with movements and a well-dressed costume. To create a more stable animation, we need to make some adjustments to the costume. One effective method is using a belt-like version that is smaller and easier to slide. ### Adjusting Particle Diameter In addition to reducing the particle diameter, we can also increase the friction coefficient to prevent sliding. Using a sewing tool, we can fix a certain point of the costume on another point. This function is similar to the "Fixed to the Virtual Model" feature. ## Using the Sewing Tool Using the sewing tool, we can find the "Fixed to the Virtual Model" tool. This tool allows us to position the costume on the virtual model, ensuring that it will not move during actions. ### Controlling Line Length The length of the line in the combinator can be controlled by the distance between two points. This control is crucial for proper costume simulation. ## Costume Adjustments and Animation Recording Additionally, we can use the sewing tool to fix the two points of the costume and the costume room. You can also choose the sewing of the line and the line of the costume. In the costume adjustment phase, you can start recording the animation. ### Observing Motion Dynamics You may notice that due to fewer stitches in this animation, the motion between the models is relatively large. For skirts made from softer fabrics and larger versions, there will be a lot of movement. Although the movements have been altered, the fabric remains in the position of the last stitch, leading to the impression that the fabric does not follow the model's body. ## Fabric Dynamics For skirts with slightly soft fabric, the movement may not be smooth enough, potentially causing the model to bend slightly. This issue is primarily due to the speed of one stitch being too fast. Without a full simulation, this can be applied to the subsequent movement. ### Playing the Animation When playing the animation, you will observe that the fabric itself is very soft and close to the body. However, the action range of the model is not closely aligned with the body. In this case, we can see that the movement remains consistent. ## Scene Change and Frame Adjustments We can change the scene change time and increase the number of action frames. Under this adjustment, the costume simulation will become more stable. Let’s take a look at the comparison. ### Frame Comparison First, change the scene time back to the original setting of 1, ensuring that the number of frames matches the original. After comparison, you will see that the animation with more frames is more suitable for real simulation. ## Impact of Material Properties The physical properties of the material will significantly affect the animation effect. The internal damping refers to the rebound coefficient of the material. When we increase this value, the material will exhibit resistance, similar to how it behaves in water, where the rebound is slower. ### Observing Waist Folds Observe the model's waist fold; when the internal damping is relatively high, it appears as though there is resistance in the environment. Additionally, the density of the fabric will also have a substantial impact on the simulation effect. ## Fabric Density The fabric of the skirt itself is polyester, which has a low density. After increasing the density, you can observe from the comparison video that as the density increases, the fabric becomes heavier and closer to the virtual model, with more pronounced folds, giving it a softer appearance. ## Conclusion In the usual production process, you can adjust the physical properties and compare them to find a more suitable fabric. Thank you for watching! Please like and subscribe to the channel. ```
